ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows wireframes of two adjacent cubes/rectangular prisms, with directional arrows drawn on the edges. Point P is at the upper left, and point Q is at the lower right. The arrows show that one may move to the right along the horizontal direction, move downward along the vertical direction, and also move along the diagonal depth edge in the same forward direction. Reasoning: From P to Q, according to the directions in the figure, the required net movements are: crossing two grid lengths to the right, for a total of 2 right moves; 1 downward move; and 1 move along the diagonal depth direction. Therefore every valid path consists of these 4 moves: {right, right, down, depth}. Different paths depend only on the order of these 4 moves, among which the two “right” moves are identical, so the number of paths is 4!/2! = 12.

method.method_draft: Interpret the drawing as a directed edge graph of two adjacent cubes/prisms. From the image, read that to get from P to Q any valid route must make exactly four directed moves: two horizontal moves to the right across the two cube lengths, one vertical move downward, and one diagonal/depth move along the slanted edge direction. The arrows show all these required move types are allowed only in the forward direction, so a path is determined solely by the order in which these four moves are taken. Count the distinct orders of the multiset {right, right, down, depth}: 4!/2! = 12.
